info.title: Lupira Contact API
info.description: Contacts, address books, and kinship backend for Lupira. Authenticate with a Bearer token issued by the OIDC provider (Authentik).

get.summary: Authenticated claims echo for dependency probes; resolves nothing, writes nothing.
The caller's resolved local identity (JIT-provisioned on first login). While no contact is linked, one carrying the login email in a readable book is linked.

post.summary: Idempotently ensure the caller has a personal address book and a linked contact of its own (one carrying the login email in a readable book, else a new one in the personal book); returns all accessible books.

put.summary: Link the caller's identity to its own contact ("this card is me") — the default focus for contact circles.

get.summary: List the address books the caller can access.

post.summary: Create an address book; the caller becomes its owner.

put.summary: Rename an address book or change its display name (owner only; merge — omitted fields are kept).

delete.summary: Delete an empty address book (owner only). 409 if it still holds contacts or groups, or is the personal book.

get.summary: List who has access to an address book and at what level (owner only).

post.summary: Grant a member access to an address book (access = owner|read-write|read; default owner).

delete.summary: Revoke a member's access to an address book (by email). 409 if it would remove the last owner.

get.summary: Search contacts by name: every query word is a name part, or the name text contains the query (case/diacritic-insensitive).

Check-in worklist: contacts ranked thinnest-first by completeness score (< maxScore, default 1 = any contact with gaps). Kind-aware (person vs organisation card). Acknowledge an inapplicable gap field by merging metadata {"completeness":{"na":["organisation"]}} so it stops counting.

post.summary: Create many contacts in one transaction (each carries its AddressBookId); returned index-for-index with the request.
Batch-match a list of names to contacts for imports: per name Matched (→contactId) / Ambiguous / NotFound, with candidate refs. Case/diacritic-insensitive full-name or all-tokens match, not phonetic.
Resolve contact ids to id + display name for contacts the caller can read (max 100). Unknown, deleted, or inaccessible ids are omitted — the existence check sibling services (cal-api attendees) run.

get.summary: Live, non-deceased contacts with a birthday across the caller's readable address books — the source of cal-api's Birthdays calendar. Year is null when only the month-day is known.
Get a single contact.

put.summary: Update a contact (merge — provided fields overwrite/append, unmentioned fields are kept).

delete.summary: Delete a contact (soft delete + tombstone). 409 if it is a member's own contact.

post.summary: Merge arbitrary JSON metadata into a contact (top-level keys overwrite). Also the channel for completeness N/A acknowledgments: {"completeness":{"na":["organisation"]}}.

Move a contact to another address book, keeping its id (so relations, group memberships and links to it survive), content and ETag. Needs write access to both books; moving it to its current book is a no-op. The sync feed reports it deleted to readers of the old book and changed to readers of the new one.

get.summary: Computed social circles (close family, extended family, friends, colleagues, household) around a focus contact — the caller's own linked contact unless focusId overrides. Degree is a closeness bucket (1 immediate, 2 two-generation kin, 3 cousin). Ended relations are excluded.

put.summary: Mark a contact as deceased (idempotent; the date may be unknown). Deceased contacts stay in the kinship graph — death is not deletion.

delete.summary: Undo a deceased marking recorded in error — the only way to clear it.

put.summary: Replace the contact's social/IM handles wholesale. Service names are canonicalized; well-known services (telegram, messenger, whatsapp…) get the profile URL derived from the handle. At most one preferred handle per service.
Set (or clear, with an empty value) the contact's avatar — a URL/media id, never image bytes.
Replace the contact's emergency-contact designation wholesale (order = priority, empty clears). A designation, not a relation kind — your emergency contact is usually also a spouse or friend.

Replace the contact's reach channels (emails + phones) wholesale (empty clears). Unlike the merge update, this can remove a channel; values are trimmed, type tokens lowercased, duplicates dropped, at most one preferred per medium.
Replace the contact's tags wholesale (empty clears). Unlike the merge update, this can remove a tag; entries are trimmed and de-duplicated case-insensitively.

get.summary: The contact's relationships, identical whichever side stores them: each entry's kind is the other contact's role relative to this one and its label this contact's own name for them. Set includeInferred=true to also return kin derived from the parent/child graph (siblings, grandparents/-children, aunts/uncles, cousins, nieces/nephews), tagged Provenance=Inferred.

post.summary: Upsert a relationship from either side: 'toContactId is this contact's kind'. The label is this contact's own name for the other; since and note are shared. Re-adding revises it and revives an ended one.

delete.summary: Remove a relationship entered by mistake, from either side. A relationship that ran its course should be ended instead.

post.summary: Mark a relationship as ended, from either side (ex-spouse, falling-out): it stays, flagged with an optional end date, and no longer asserts current kinship. Re-adding it revives it.

get.summary: List groups (personal groupings + organizations) in an address book.

post.summary: Create a group. kind = group|organization (an employer is an organization-kind group).

Move a group to another address book, keeping its id, name, kind, members and roles. Needs write access to both books; moving it to its current book is a no-op. includeMembers also moves the member contacts living in the group's current book; members in other books stay put.
Add a contact to a group; for an organization, role is the title held there (re-adding updates it).

delete.summary: Remove a contact from a group.

get.summary: Every relationship whose two contacts the caller can read. Per contact, GET /contacts/{id}/relations gives the view from that contact.
Where the contact lives, holidays and works: current residencies first, then the most recent move-in first.

post.summary: Start a residency at a LupiraGeoApi place (resolve the address there first — no free text). Refused when it overlaps another of the contact's residencies at the same place.

put.summary: Correct a residency as entered: place, type, label and period, wholesale. A move is told with move-out or POST /moves instead.

delete.summary: Erase a residency entered by mistake. One that ended should be moved out of instead.

post.summary: End a residency: the contact moved out on the given date (a year, year-month, or day).

get.summary: Every residency of a contact the caller can read — who lives, holidays and works where.

post.summary: Several contacts move together: each one's current residencies at fromPlaceId end on movedIn, and a residency at toPlaceId starts then. All or nothing. Returns the new residencies.

get.summary: The door and gate codes at a place. Visible while the caller can read a contact currently living there; otherwise 404.

put.summary: Add or replace a code (the client mints codeId). Needs write on a contact currently living there.

delete.summary: Remove a code. Needs write on a contact currently living there.

get.summary: Contacts for offline mirrors: every contact the caller can read that changed since the cursor, with its section guards, plus tombstone ids for contacts deleted or no longer readable (incl. moved to an unreadable address book). Omit since for a full sync; loop while hasMore, persisting cursor between calls. reset = drop the local mirror first.
Same feed as GET /sync/contacts, kept for existing installs.

Relationships for offline mirrors: those whose two contacts the caller can read that changed since the cursor (directly, or through a contact on them), plus tombstone ids for removed or no-longer-visible ones. Omit since for a full sync; loop while hasMore, persisting cursor between calls. reset = drop the local mirror first.

Residencies for offline mirrors: those of contacts the caller can read that changed since the cursor (directly, or through their contact), plus tombstone ids for removed or no-longer-visible ones. Omit since for a full sync; loop while hasMore, persisting cursor between calls. reset = drop the local mirror first.

Door and gate codes for offline mirrors, per place the caller can see a current resident of. Tombstones are place ids no longer visible. Omit since for a full sync; loop while hasMore, persisting cursor between calls. reset = drop the local mirror first.
Every address book the caller can read, with their access level. Always a complete snapshot (reset, no cursor): replace the local copy on each call.
Every contact group in an address book the caller can read. Always a complete snapshot (reset, no cursor): replace the local copy on each call.
Snapshot of the caller's address books + contact groups for mirror reconciliation (no cursor — fetch once per sync cycle and diff locally).

Access.description: A principal's permission on a collection. `Owner` adds member-management + delete rights over `ReadWrite`.

label.description: This contact's own name for the other, e.g. "dad". The other side keeps its own.

since.description: When the relationship began, if a precise date is known.

note.description: Free-text note about the relationship (how/where it started); fuzzy periods that aren't a precise date go here.

AddContactRelationRequest.description: Upserts a relationship from either side: "Guid AddContactRelationRequest.ToContactId is this contact's ContactRelationKind AddContactRelationRequest.Kind".

isPersonal.description: True only for the caller's own personal book — another member's shared personal book has the same slug.

AddressBookDto.description: An address book the caller can access, with their access level.

CircleKind.description: An inferred social cohort around a focus contact (computed on read, never stored).

CircleMemberDto.description:
`Degree` is a pragmatic closeness bucket (1 = immediate, 2 = two-generation kin, 3 = cousin), not
        consanguinity. `Kind` is null when the membership makes no kinship claim (household co-residency).

CompletenessGap.description: A field the record is missing or thin on, with its rubric weight (heavier = ask first).

CompletenessScore.description:
How well-documented a record is: `Score` 0..1 (Σ weight·presence / Σ weight), the unmet
            fields ranked by missing mass (weight·absence, largest first), and the rubric version that produced it.
            `null` (not this type) means "not applicable".

ContactAddressType.description: How a contact uses a place: where they live, a vacation home, where they work, or something else.

ContactBirthdayDto.description:
A contact's birthday for cal-api's Birthdays calendar. int? ContactBirthdayDto.Year is null when only the
            month-day is known (see PartialDate).

ContactCirclesDto.description:
Computed social circles around a focus contact. Always contains every CircleKind, possibly empty;
            a contact may appear in several circles.

avatarRef.description: Pointer to an avatar image (URL/media id), never bytes.

emergencyContactIds.description: Ordered designation (first = highest priority) — who to call about this person, not a kinship.

oneOf.description: How well-documented this contact is. Drives contact-enrichment ranking (completeness × relevance).

version.description: Stream version — the offline clients' optimistic-versioning surface (`Etag` stays content-derived).

ContactGroupDto.description: A contact group (personal grouping or organization) and its current members.

ContactGroupKind.description: A personal grouping (Friends/Family/Colleagues) vs a company/institution. An employer is membership in an `Organization`-kind group.

ContactKind.description:
What the contact card represents. A business/venue (a provider referenced from
            bookings, say) is an `Organization`: no birthday, employer, or kinship applies. `Individual` is ordinal 0
            so pre-existing events replay as persons.

ContactNameMatch.description:
Resolution of one input name. On `Matched`, `ContactId` is set; `Candidates` always lists
            the considered contacts (capped) so the caller can disambiguate.

ContactReachChannel.description:
A way to reach a contact — an email address or phone number — with an open string? ContactReachChannel.Type token
            (well-known: home/work/cell/fax/pager/other) and a per-medium bool ContactReachChannel.Preferred flag. A record so event
            payloads stay immutable.

ContactRef.description: A lightweight contact reference (id + display name) — a resolve candidate.

since.description: When the relationship began, if a precise date is known.

ended.description: The relationship ran its course (ex-spouse); it remains for history but asserts no current kinship.

ContactRelationEntryDto.description:
One relationship as seen from the viewed contact, identical whichever side stores it. ContactRelationKind ContactRelationEntryDto.Kind is the OTHER
            contact's role relative to the viewed one and string? ContactRelationEntryDto.Label the viewed contact's own name for them; since, note and the
            ended flag belong to the relationship and read the same from both sides. RelationProvenance ContactRelationEntryDto.Provenance distinguishes stored
            relationships from kin derived off the parent/child graph (returned only when inferred relations are requested).

ContactSocialProfileDto.description:
A contact's social/IM handle as published. Service and handle are guaranteed non-empty —
            `SetProfilesAsync` rejects the write otherwise.

ContactSocialProfileInput.description:
A social/IM handle as submitted. `Url` is derived from the handle for well-known services when
            omitted; `Preferred` defaults to false.

ContactSyncChange.description: A changed contact: the full DTO plus its section guards.

CreateAddressBookRequest.description: Create an address book; the caller becomes its owner.

sourceKey.description:
Client-chosen stable key that pins the contact's identity (offline clients mint a UUIDv7): a
            replayed create with the same key returns the existing contact instead of duplicating it.

oneOf.description: Individual (default) or Organization — a business/venue card that skips person-only enrichment.

CreateContactRequest.description:
Create a contact via REST/MCP. No `FullName` — the display name is composed from the structured parts.
            An employer is set separately as membership in an `organization`-kind contact group.

CreateContactsBatchRequest.description:
Create many contacts in one transaction (each carries its own `AddressBookId`). Returned contacts
            align index-for-index with `Contacts`. For bulk imports instead of many single `create_contact` calls.

DisplayNameFormat.description: How a contact's DisplayName renders. Rendering-only — excluded from the content hash. `Full` is ordinal 0 so old events replay to today's behavior.

EndContactRelationRequest.description: Ends a relation (relationship ran its course — the edge stays, flagged). Removal is for edges entered by mistake.

FuzzyDate.description:
A date known to year, year-month, or full-day precision — the precision itself carries the certainty
            ("2015" means "sometime in 2015"). Used for residency boundaries.
            int FuzzyDate.Year is always present; int? FuzzyDate.Day requires int? FuzzyDate.Month. Distinct from
            PartialDate, which models the opposite case (year unknown, month-day known).

GapSeverity.description: A field is fully present, weak/partial (0.5), or absent.

GrantOwnerRequest.description:
Grant a member access to a container, identified by their login `Email` (provisioned if they have
            not logged in yet). `Access` is `owner` (default), `read-write`, or `read` — case-insensitive.

GroupMemberDto.description:
A contact's membership in a group. `Role` is the title held in an organization (null for personal
            groupings); `Since`/`Until` bound the tenure when known.

contactId.description: The caller's own contact ("this card is me"), when linked — the default circles focus.

MeDto.description:
The resolved local identity of the caller: the stable Guid MeDto.PrincipalId plus current
            email/display name — the same identity shape (`principalId`/`email`/`displayName`) the
            platform uses everywhere it returns a person.

addressBookId.description: The address book to move the group into.

includeMembers.description: Also move the member contacts that live in the group's current book; members in other books stay put.

membersMoved.description: Members moved with the group (always 0 without `includeMembers`).

membersSkipped.description: Live members left where they are because they live in another book.

addressBookId.description: The address book to move the contact into.

fromPlaceId.description: The place they leave; omit when nobody leaves anywhere (a new vacation home, say).

MoveRequest.description:
Several contacts move together, e.g. a family: each one's current residencies at `FromPlaceId` end on
            `MovedIn`, and a new residency at `ToPlaceId` starts then.

NameMatchOutcome.description:
Per-name match outcome, compared case-, diacritic- and punctuation-insensitively. `Matched` = exactly one
            contact whose full name form (given+family, given+middle+family, nickname, nickname+family or display name) equals
            the query, or else the lone contact holding every token of a multi-token query; `Ambiguous` = several such
            contacts, or a lone token hit on a one-token query; `NotFound` = no contact holds every query token.

OwnerGrantDto.description: The result of granting a member access to a container: who now has what access on which container.

PartialDate.description:
A calendar date that may omit the year — a birthday is often known only as a month-day.
            int PartialDate.Month and int PartialDate.Day are always present; int? PartialDate.Year is null when unknown.
            Canonical text is `yyyy-MM-dd` with a year, else `--MM-dd`; other wire formats are the serializers' concern.

PingDto.description:
The claims a caller's token resolved to, echoed for cross-service auth-seam probes.
            Returning the audiences (not a bare 200) lets a failing consumer see which half of the seam
            is misconfigured.

PlaceEntryDto.description: How to get in at a place: its door and gate codes, shared by everyone living there.

ReachMedium.description: The medium a reach channel uses. Social/IM handles are modeled separately as ContactSocialProfile.

RelationProvenance.description: Whether a resolved relation was stored explicitly or derived from the kinship graph.

RelationshipDto.description:
A relationship between two contacts: "`HighId` is `LowId`'s `Kind`". Low/High is the ids' ordinal
            order, not which side stated it. Each side has its own label (its word for the other); the rest is shared.

ResidencyDto.description: A contact's tie to a geo place over a period. Current = today inside [movedIn, movedOut]; null ends are open.

placeId.description: A LupiraGeoApi place id — resolve the address there first; no free text.

ResidencyRequest.description: A residency as stated: start one, or correct one wholesale.

ResolveContactsByNameRequest.description:
Batch-match a list of free-text names to existing contacts (import disambiguation). Optionally scope to
            one address book; otherwise all the caller's accessible books.

occurredAt.description:
Client wall-clock of the edit, for last-writer-wins conflict resolution of the core fields.
            Omitted ⇒ server receive time.

ReviseContactRequest.description: Update an existing contact by merge: a provided scalar overwrites, provided reach channels/tags are unioned onto the existing values (deduped), and any field left null keeps its current value. Enrichment never wipes what it didn't mention. Use `PUT /contacts/{id}/channels` to remove channels. The address book isn't changeable here.

SectionGuardDto.description:
One section's last-writer guard: the (occurredAt, commandId) of the write that owns its current
            value. Offline clients seed their local guards from these so a pending edit on one section never blocks —
            and is never clobbered by — fresher server state on another.

SectionGuardsDto.description:
Per-section guards for a contact. `Core` covers the whole ContactFields (name/channels/tags/
            notes… — channel and tag writes ride the same revision event); the rest map 1:1 to their write endpoints.

occurredAt.description: Client wall-clock of the edit, for last-writer-wins conflict resolution. Omitted ⇒ server receive time.

SetContactAvatarRequest.description: Sets (or clears, when null/empty) a contact's avatar — a URL/media id, never image bytes.

occurredAt.description: Client wall-clock of the edit, for last-writer-wins conflict resolution. Omitted ⇒ server receive time.

SetContactChannelsRequest.description:
Wholesale replacement of a contact's reach channels — emails and phones (empty clears). Unlike
            `ReviseContact`, which only unions, this can remove a channel. Values are trimmed, type tokens lowercased,
            duplicates (by medium + value) dropped; at most one preferred channel per medium.

occurredAt.description: Client wall-clock of the edit, for last-writer-wins conflict resolution. Omitted ⇒ server receive time.

SetContactProfilesRequest.description:
Wholesale replacement of a contact's social/IM handles. For well-known services (telegram, messenger,
            whatsapp…) the profile URL is derived from the handle when omitted.

occurredAt.description: Client wall-clock of the edit, for last-writer-wins conflict resolution. Omitted ⇒ server receive time.

SetContactTagsRequest.description:
Wholesale replacement of a contact's tags (empty clears). Unlike `ReviseContact`,
            which only unions, this can remove a tag. Entries are trimmed and de-duplicated case-insensitively.

occurredAt.description: Client wall-clock of the edit, for last-writer-wins conflict resolution. Omitted ⇒ server receive time.

SetDeceasedRequest.description: Marks a contact as deceased; the date may be unknown.

SetEmergencyContactsRequest.description: Wholesale replacement of a contact's emergency-contact designation; order = priority, empty clears.

SetMyContactRequest.description: Links the caller's identity to its own contact ("this card is me") — the default circles focus.

SyncContainersResponse.description:
Snapshot of the caller's containers. Address books are plain documents (no cursor); groups are
            event-sourced but small and fully replaced each cycle — both are fetched once per sync cycle and diffed
            against the mirror.

SyncPageOfAddressBookDto.description: One page of a `/sync/*` feed. `reset` starts a full sync: rows the full sync never mentions are gone.

SyncPageOfContactGroupDto.description: One page of a `/sync/*` feed. `reset` starts a full sync: rows the full sync never mentions are gone.

SyncPageOfContactSyncChange.description: One page of a `/sync/*` feed. `reset` starts a full sync: rows the full sync never mentions are gone.

SyncPageOfPlaceEntryDto.description: One page of a `/sync/*` feed. `reset` starts a full sync: rows the full sync never mentions are gone.

SyncPageOfRelationshipDto.description: One page of a `/sync/*` feed. `reset` starts a full sync: rows the full sync never mentions are gone.

SyncPageOfResidencyDto.description: One page of a `/sync/*` feed. `reset` starts a full sync: rows the full sync never mentions are gone.

UpdateAddressBookRequest.description: Update an address book by merge: a provided slug or display name overwrites, null keeps the current value.

Bearer.description: OIDC bearer token. Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
